body: I can take a look into this. When the two property values are the same we can probably skip merging them. What would you expect to happen when you have mixture of associative, and non associative settings?

> What would you expect to happen when you have mixture of associative, and non associative settings?

Probably the associative one should take precedence since it would have extra options.
Configuration merge is super painful, sometimes I want to merge (eg. Auth Adapters) but many times I wish it just overwrote the old keys instead, e.g. with Crud.Crud actions config
Well we can't have it both ways :(

This reminds me a lot of the old Model arrays :)

Would a config object resolve this kind of situations?

Maybe it should always overwrite when defining the same property in a child class (Default PHP behavior). 

If you wish to use/change some of the values set in a parent class you could do the merging yourself in Model::initialize() / constructor? 

Less magic, easier to understand for newcomers - and no real drawbacks I can think of.
:+1: for overwriting things rather than merging :)
I its a boolean decision :+1:  for overriting too.

If I'm understanding you correctly, the merged result of settings in a component's config should reflect the top most config values only?

In the following example:

``` php
// In a parent class.
[
  'Crud.Crud' => [
    'foo' => 'bar',
    'active'
  ],
  'DebugKit.Toolbar' => ['enabled' => true]
]

// In a child class
[
  'Crud.Crud' => [
    'foo' => 'updated value'
  ]
]
```

The merged result would be:

``` php
[
  'Crud.Crud' => [
    'foo' => 'updated value',
  ],
  'DebugKit.Toolbar' => ['enabled' => true]
]
```

This is a change in historical behavior, but I'm ok with that if we think the new behavior will be easier to grok and provides the value that comes with merging properties.

I actually meant it should behave like native  php. It's possible to merge/modify parent config with other config data yourself in Child class' construct if that is desired behavior.

Does it really add value to magically automerge config?
Now I understand what you meant, Mark. And yes, I think that would be a good way to handle it.

Regarding automagically merging configurations, I feel the same way @biesbjerg does.

In fact I've had a very long discussion about that [here](https://github.com/kamisama/Cake-Resque/pull/28#issuecomment-26563015) which can be summarized by this two comments [[1]](https://github.com/kamisama/Cake-Resque/pull/28#issuecomment-24701485) and [[2]](https://github.com/kamisama/Cake-Resque/pull/28#issuecomment-24706249).

It is always better to let the children handle the merge because it will always be ok, but automagically merging will never be 100% correct for everyone.
Ok, then I'll update the merging code to work like https://github.com/cakephp/cakephp/issues/2914#issuecomment-36375178
Hmm... Won't that cause problems if using 'className' to alias objects?
Maybe, I can make the change and we can see what happens :smile:

issue.body:
As per #2914. This removes deep merging from the MergeVariablesTrait. Instead only the top level keys are merged for associative properties. 
List style properties are still simply merged.

Hopefully, this new behavior makes merged properties simpler to understand with more predictable results.
